transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
My ankles are swollen, both of them.
When did you first notice the swelling in your ankles?
About four weeks back, I think.
Have you ever had any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
No, I've never had a bad reaction to medicines.
How much is the swelling affecting your day-to-day activities?
My sister had heart failure, that's what worries me.
Can you tell me about any medicines you're taking at the moment, including any that are new or have changed?
They upped my amlodipine a while back.
Have you ever had any operations?
No, I've never had an operation.
How bad would you say the swelling is? Is it mild, moderate, severe, or you're not sure?
Mildly uncomfortable, about three out of ten.
Have you noticed anything else going on along with the swelling?
No, I can lie flat without getting breathless.
Is there anything that seems to make the swelling worse?
It's worse by the evening, better in the mornings.
How would you describe what your ankles feel like when they're swollen?
Shoes feel tight by teatime.
Is there anything else about your past health—like other illnesses or ongoing conditions—that you'd like to add?
My husband's waiting outside; he always comes with me.
Is there anything else you'd like to add about your medicines—anything new or changed recently?
I take a little water tablet each morning.
Has anything changed lately in your usual daily routine?
I put my feet up in the afternoons now.
Is there anything else about your past health that you’d like to add?
I've got high blood pressure.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
